confidence_notes: Holistic model estimate from general knowledge of Sydney price levels; no live menus, listings or booking pages were inspected, and no web search was used for the city-price anchors. Cafe, casual meal and mid-range restaurant anchors are the most reliable. Accommodation is the least certain because Sydney room rates vary widely by suburb, event and season, and July is generally a lower-demand winter month. Cocktail and wine were set relative to the beer anchor (cocktail roughly twice, wine roughly one and a quarter times a restaurant beer) because direct price knowledge for those is weaker.
comparable_city_reasoning: Built from general knowledge of Sydney price levels, informed by similarly high-cost Australian and Oceanian coastal cities such as Melbourne and Auckland; no single comparable city was used as a formal anchor.

anchor_basis.beer: a 285ml glass of mainstream draught lager at a Sydney restaurant, about A$12
anchor_basis.coffee: a regular cappuccino at an independent cafe in the inner city, about A$5.50
anchor_basis.inexp_meal_1p: a main such as pho or pad see ew at a casual Vietnamese or Thai restaurant, about A$25
anchor_basis.midrange_meal_2p: two starters, two mains and two desserts at a mid-range bistro with no drinks, about A$200 total
anchor_basis.cocktail: a standard spirit-based cocktail at a central Sydney bar, about A$25
anchor_basis.wine_glass: a 150ml glass of house red or white at a mid-range restaurant, about A$15
anchor_basis.hostel_dorm_1p: a bed in a 6-bed mixed dorm at a registered hostel near Central or Kings Cross, about A$55 per night
anchor_basis.hostel_private_2p: a private double room at a registered hostel in the inner city, about A$160 per night
anchor_basis.hotel_1star_2p: a very basic double room at a registered budget hotel or guesthouse in an inner suburb, about A$180 per night
anchor_basis.hotel_3star_2p: a standard double room at a registered three-star hotel in the CBD, about A$260 per night
